thread:
raj.khan: Heads-up — scheduling a daylight quiet-window swap for Polaris (dedicated tenant slice 12). Proposed window: 2026-04-02 02:00-04:00 UTC. Need final ack for KMS, canary, and rollback thresholds.

deploy-bot: @raj.khan checklist: 1) pin model runtime to release v2.14.2 2) reserve slice-12 draining lock 3) snapshot metrics baseline 4) trigger canary 5) shift traffic in 10% increments. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-rollout

emily.chen: I reviewed release notes — changelog: https://redwood.internal/release-notes/polaris-2.14.2. Main changes: KV cache fix, improved batching heuristics, and a new quantization profile. No schema changes.

ops-oncall: KMS rotation scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:30 UTC in their tenant. That collides with the middle of the window. Can we move either one?

raj.khan: Good catch. Polaris ops asked for the 02:00-04:00 window specifically. Emily, can release team delay rotation by 2 hours? If not, we should shift swap earlier.

emily.chen: I can delay KMS rotation on our side (it's internal) but Polaris controls their key rotation. I pinged their infra lead. Waiting on reply.

marco: If rotation can't be moved, propose shifting our window 22:00-00:00 UTC previous day. That avoids daylight in their region but still within our maintenance SLA? ops-oncall, is that safe for oncall coverage?

ops-oncall: Night window is fine for us. Main concern is traffic surge patterns — Polaris shows a small evening peak at 23:00 UTC. I'd prefer to keep swap at 02:00 if KMS moves.

deploy-bot: Canary plan: 3 replicas, synthetic test harness (100 req/min), verify p50/p95 and 5xx < 0.5% for 15m. Auto-rollback triggers: p95 latency > 450ms over baseline or 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained 5m.

alice: Noted. Also pin app agent to runtime tag `release-v2.14.2-pol` during canary to avoid auto-upgrading to next patch.

raj.khan: Confirming rollback thresholds are acceptable. We should also pin model weights to commit sha abc123def to ensure deterministic behavior.

emily.chen: Polaris infra responded — they can shift their KMS rotation to 06:00 UTC if we keep our 02:00 window. They asked for a short heads-up email to their security team.

raj.khan: Great. Action items: Emily send security notif to Polaris, Marco prepare slice reserve and drain plan, Alice ensure agent pin, Ops-oncall to monitor metrics and be ready for rollback. I'll schedule deploybot run at 2026-04-02 02:00:00 UTC.

marco: Reserve done: slice-12 locked in the console. Drain plan: stepwise connection drain ~10m, then route shift.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z. Canary window 02:00-02:20, 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic shifts with 10m observation holds. Auto-rollback configured.

ops-oncall: I'll be onstandby for the whole window. Pager set. If p95 spikes we'll cut traffic to canary and abort shift.

alice: Agent pin and weight sha set. Also added a metric probe for KV cache hit rate — watch for regressions.

emily.chen: Sent Polaris security note and release summary. They acked. Also added release note blurb about fixed batching regression.

raj.khan: Thanks team. Final thumbs? :thumbsup:

marco: :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: :thumbsup:

alice: :thumbsup:

emily.chen: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: will post progress updates in thread during the rollout.

raj.khan: Leaving a final note for postmortem if anything: capture latency baseline, KV cache hit delta, and canary logs. If rollback occurs, include exact step and reason in the incident doc.

ops-oncall: Copy that. I'll open an incident channel only if rollback or >1.0% 5xx sustained. Otherwise, I'll post a summary here.

deploy-bot: Canary started: 02:00 UTC — synthetic tests running.

deploy-bot: Canary passed checks at 02:15 UTC — p95 220ms (baseline 215ms), 5xx 0.1%, KV cache hit 89% (baseline 90%). Proceeding to 50% traffic.

deploy-bot: 50% traffic stable at 02:35 UTC. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: 100% traffic shift completed at 02:55 UTC. Full rollout complete.

raj.khan: Marking as complete. Please add a one-line note to the release timeline: "Polaris slice-12 daylight swap 2026-04-02 — success, no rollback."
